Question: Do you believe that you can manifest anything that you want into existence if you believe hard enough?
Answer: While I strongly believe in the power of positive thinking, I do not think if if you wish strongly enough for a chicken sandwich to appear it will pop into existence as if summoned by a genie. I do feel that whatever energy you put out in life will attract a like type of energy. I know someone that always, always thinks the worst of any situation. You know what? Often they get a terrible outcome. If you bring your car to the mechanic enough they will find something wrong with it. I stay away from negativity as much as possible. Bad things happen sure, but if I have no power to change it, I don’t waste my energy worrying about it and I just move on. Things will turn around eventually and if there’s anything I can do to solve the problem I do it. Keeping positive isn’t a magical shield or the ability to wish yourself a winning lottery ticket. It’s just being open to the fact that things might be ok, and being open to opportunities when they arise. This is powerful in my opinion and changed my life. A small example. I was at a Guns N Roses concert with a friend and we were walking to our cheap, upper level seats when a young girl asked my friend a question while holding a clipboard. He dismissed her out of hand, assuming she was trying to sell him something. When she approached me I stopped for a second to listen to her. She was with the concert and was upgrading people to the lower level to fill seats for something they were filming. SCORE! So I gave up a second of my life to hear someone out and got incredible seats for an incredible concert. My friend was thankful for my open mindedness for sure.

Question: How are CMYK and RGB, both primary colours?
Answer: Most of us learn in Kindergarten that the primary colors are red, yellow and blue. You use these three primary colors to mix up almost any other color you want. In art school they advance this further by listing the secondary (Green, Orange and Violet) and tertiary colors (Yellow Orange, Orange Red, Red Violet, Blue Violet, etc.) that result from mixing the primaries. When you mention primary colors anyone outside the printing industry is going to think in these terms. So how are CMYK and RGB primary colors? Well the definition of primary colors is simply a group or set of colors that can be combined to to produce a gamut or range of colors. Commercial printing mostly revolves around 2 sets of colors. CMYK and RGB. CMYK or 4 color process printing combines Cyan, Yellow, Magenta and Black (yes K is Black) to mix up the gamut of colors needed for color printing. Every shade you see on the printed page is made of a mixture of these four primary colors. RGB is a mixture of Red, Green and Blue and they mix in much the same way as CMYK does to create every shade within it's gamut. RGB has a much larger gamut and much richer colors. In each printing system they are both considered the primary colors since you use that specific set to create the colors within it's range. So that's how CMYK and RGB can be primary colors. Question: What is the game Mafia?
Answer: When I was a kid growing up on Long Island NY in the 1970s I spent many an afternoon after school playing the game “Mafia” with my friends. The game we called mafia was a simple one. A kid would take ahold of a ball, most often a football. Then the other kids would circle around him. The kid holding the ball would then throw the ball straight up in the air. All the kids then would leap at the now falling ball trying to catch it. Whomever caught the ball would then be pounced upon by the other kids and everyone would try to take the ball away from him. If the guy with the ball got out of the pile he won. It kind of looked like this but less orderly. (Image source: Google) No idea how or why we called it mafia. It was something the older kids called it and we carried it forward. Looking back we might have been a little crazy. Maybe sometime I’ll get to write an answer about our garbage dumpster battle-royale last man standing matches.
